speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the Penis and Digit.

Based on the patient's history of heavy smoking, African ancestry, and non-healing, painless, crusted lesions on the genitalia and distal extremity that failed previous treatments for syphilis and eczema, the clinical picture is highly suggestive of invasive squamous cell carcinoma, a malignancy strongly associated with HPV infection and tobacco use in high-risk populations.
